topics.title: Forms: form, label, input & Submitting
topics.summary: The form element collects user input; label and name make controls usable and submittable.
topics.description:
A **form** collects data from the user and sends it to a server (or handles it with JavaScript). It is the basis of logins, search boxes, checkouts and contact pages.

### Core pieces
- `<form action="/submit" method="post">` - the container. `action` is the URL that receives the data; `method` is `get` (data in the URL, for searches) or `post` (data in the request body, for sensitive or large data).
- `<label for="email">` - a caption **linked** to a control by id. Clicking the label focuses the input, and screen readers announce it. Labels are essential for accessibility.
- `<input id="email" name="email">` - a control. The **`name`** is the key under which the value is sent; an input without a name is **not submitted**.
- `<button type="submit">` or `<input type="submit">` - sends the form.

### Two ways to link a label
```html
<label for="user">Username</label>
<input id="user" name="user">

<label>Username <input name="user"></label>   <!-- wrapping -->
```

### Form flow
1. User fills controls.
2. On submit the browser validates (see validation topic).
3. The browser sends `name=value` pairs to `action` and loads the response - unless JavaScript calls `event.preventDefault()`.

### Button types
`type="submit"` (default inside forms), `type="reset"`, `type="button"` (does nothing by itself - use for JS actions).
keyPoints: action = where to send; method = get or post.
Every control needs a name to be submitted.
label for="id" links text to a control; always provide labels.
button type defaults to submit inside a form.
Use preventDefault() when handling submit in JavaScript.
pitfalls: Inputs without name attributes - the value is never sent.
Using placeholder instead of a label.
A button inside a form defaults to submit, accidentally submitting the form.

interview.q: Difference between GET and POST?
interview.a: GET appends data to the URL (visible, bookmarkable, for searches); POST sends data in the request body (for sensitive or large data and changes on the server).

interview.q: Why is the name attribute important on inputs?
interview.a: The name is the key in the submitted data; controls without a name are not sent.

interview.q: Why use label elements?
interview.a: They give inputs accessible names, enlarge the click target and improve usability.

topics.title: Text-like Input Types
topics.summary: text, password, email, number, tel, url and search give the right keyboard and validation.
topics.description:
The `<input>` element changes behaviour with its `type` attribute. Choosing the correct type gives you free validation and the correct mobile keyboard.

| type | Use | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `text` | Single line text | default |
| `password` | Secret text | characters hidden |
| `email` | Email address | validates @ format, email keyboard |
| `number` | Numbers | `min`, `max`, `step`, spinner |
| `tel` | Phone numbers | numeric keypad, no format validation |
| `url` | Web address | must be a valid absolute URL |
| `search` | Search query | may show a clear (x) button |

### Useful attributes
- `placeholder` - hint text (never a substitute for a label).
- `value` - default value.
- `min` / `max` / `step` - numeric range.
- `minlength` / `maxlength` - text length.
- `autocomplete` - help the browser autofill: `email`, `username`, `current-password`, `new-password`.
- `inputmode` - choose the virtual keyboard (`numeric`, `decimal`, `email`...).

### Number vs tel
Use `type="number"` for quantities you add or compare. Use `type="tel"` (or text + pattern) for IDs, phone numbers and OTPs - you do not want a spinner and mathematical behaviour.

### Security
A password field only **hides the characters**. Always send passwords over HTTPS and never store them in plain text.
keyPoints: type chooses control behaviour, validation and mobile keyboard.
email, url, number validate automatically on submit.
Use tel (not number) for phone numbers and codes.
placeholder is a hint, not a label.
Set autocomplete tokens to help password managers.
pitfalls: Using type="number" for phone numbers or credit cards.
Relying on placeholder as the only label.
Disabling paste or autocomplete on password fields.

examples.html: (try an invalid email or a number above 5)
examples.explanation: Invalid values are blocked by the browser before the submit event fires.

interview.q: What is the benefit of type="email" over type="text"?
interview.a: Built-in format validation, an email-friendly keyboard on mobile and autofill support.

interview.q: Why is type="number" a poor choice for phone numbers?
interview.a: It adds spinners, strips leading zeros and rejects characters like + or spaces. Use tel or text with pattern.

interview.q: Does type="password" encrypt the data?
interview.a: No, it only masks the characters on screen. Use HTTPS to protect data in transit.

topics.title: Radio, Checkbox, Select & Datalist
topics.summary: Let users choose from options: one of many (radio, select), many (checkbox), or suggestions (datalist).
topics.description:
### Radio buttons
Choose **exactly one** option from a group. Radios are grouped by sharing the same **`name`**. Each needs its own `value`.

```html
<input type="radio" id="m" name="gender" value="male"> <label for="m">Male</label>
<input type="radio" id="f" name="gender" value="female"> <label for="f">Female</label>
```

### Checkboxes
Choose **any number** (zero, one or many). Checked ones are submitted. Use `checked` for a default. Checkboxes sharing a name submit multiple values.

### select + option
A drop-down list. `<option value="..">` holds the value; `<optgroup label="..">` groups options; `multiple` allows multi-select; `size` shows a list box.

### datalist
`<input list="countries">` plus `<datalist id="countries">` gives **suggestions** while typing - but the user may still type something else.

| | select | datalist |
|---|---|---|
| Free text allowed | No | Yes |
| Must pick from list | Yes | No |
| Best for | fixed choice | suggestions |

### Accessibility tips
- Wrap related radios/checkboxes in a `<fieldset>` with a `<legend>` (see next topic).
- Always connect each choice to a label so the text is clickable.
- For long lists of yes/no choices consider a checkbox group; for 2 mutually exclusive options a radio group.
keyPoints: Radios with the same name form one group; only one selected.
Checkboxes allow multiple selections.
select = fixed list; datalist = suggestions with free text.
Use optgroup to group long option lists.
Each radio/checkbox needs its own label.
pitfalls: Giving radios different name values - they will not exclude each other.
Forgetting value on options so text is sent instead.
Making placeholder-like first option required without disabled/empty value.

examples.title: All choice controls
examples.html:
Gender
Hobbies
(submit to see selections)

interview.q: How do you group radio buttons?
interview.a: Give them the same name attribute; the browser allows only one of them to be selected.

interview.q: Select vs datalist?
interview.a: select forces a choice from the list; datalist offers suggestions but still allows free text.

interview.q: How do you let a select accept several values?
interview.a: Add the multiple attribute to select (and use name with the values submitted as multiple entries).

topics.title: Date, Time, Color, Range, File & Hidden Inputs
topics.summary: Built-in pickers: date, time, month, week, datetime-local, color, range, file and hidden.
topics.description:
HTML5 added many input types that show native pickers, so you rarely need a JavaScript date library for simple forms.

| type | Control | Submitted value format |
|---|---|---|
| `date` | Calendar picker | `2026-10-14` |
| `time` | Time picker | `14:30` |
| `datetime-local` | Date + time | `2026-10-14T14:30` |
| `month` | Month & year | `2026-10` |
| `week` | Week of year | `2026-W42` |
| `color` | Colour chooser | `#e34c26` |
| `range` | Slider | a number |
| `file` | File upload | file(s) |
| `hidden` | Invisible value | any string |

### Constraints
`min`, `max`, `step` work on date/time/number/range. Example: `<input type="date" min="2026-01-01">`.

### file
- `accept=".pdf,image/*"` filters selectable types.
- `multiple` allows many files.
- `capture` hints the camera on mobile.
- The form needs `enctype="multipart/form-data"` and `method="post"` to upload.

### range
Has no visible value by default; show it with `<output>` and a few lines of JS.

### hidden
Sends data the user does not see (a CSRF token, a record id). It is **not secure** - users can edit it in DevTools.

### Browser support
All modern browsers support these pickers, but their UI differs. The submitted value format is always the same.
keyPoints: date, time, month, week and datetime-local give native pickers.
Submitted values use fixed ISO-style formats.
range needs output/JS to display its value.
file uploads need method=post and multipart/form-data.
hidden inputs are not secret - never trust them.
pitfalls: Using type="date" values assuming a local format like DD/MM/YYYY.
Forgetting enctype for file upload so only the file name is sent.
Putting sensitive data in hidden inputs.

examples.title: Pickers, slider and colour
examples.html: (submit to see values)

interview.q: What format does input type="date" submit?
interview.a: ISO format YYYY-MM-DD, regardless of the display format in the picker.

interview.q: What is needed to upload files with a form?
interview.a: method="post", enctype="multipart/form-data" and an input type="file".

interview.q: Is a hidden input secure?
interview.a: No. It is only invisible; users can see and change it with DevTools, so always validate on the server.

topics.title: textarea, button & fieldset/legend
topics.summary: Multi-line text, proper buttons and grouping related controls with fieldset and legend.
topics.description:
### textarea
Multi-line text input. Unlike `<input>` it has a closing tag and its default text goes **between** the tags.

```html
<textarea name="msg" rows="5" cols="40" maxlength="300" placeholder="Your message"></textarea>
```

- `rows` / `cols` set initial size (or use CSS `width`/`height`).
- `wrap`, `maxlength`, `readonly`, `required` are supported.
- Whitespace inside the tags is preserved, so avoid indenting the content.

### button vs input
| | `<button>` | `<input type="submit">` |
|---|---|---|
| Content | any HTML (icons, text) | only the `value` text |
| Types | submit, reset, button | submit, reset, button |

Prefer `<button>`: it is more flexible. Always set `type` explicitly (`type="button"` for non-submitting buttons).

### fieldset and legend
`<fieldset>` groups related controls; `<legend>` is its caption. Assistive tech reads the legend before each control inside, which is critical for radio groups ("Gender, Male radio button").

```html
<fieldset>
  <legend>Contact Info</legend>
  ...controls...
</fieldset>
```

A `disabled` attribute on the fieldset disables **all** controls inside at once. Browsers draw a border by default; style it with CSS.
keyPoints: textarea is multi-line; its default text goes between the tags.
button can hold HTML; set its type explicitly.
fieldset groups controls; legend is the group caption.
disabled on a fieldset disables all its controls.
pitfalls: Indenting textarea content - the spaces become part of the value.
Leaving button without type inside a form.
Skipping fieldset/legend for radio groups.

examples.title: Grouped contact form
examples.html:
Contact Info 
(submit)

interview.q: Why use fieldset and legend?
interview.a: They semantically group related controls and give the group an accessible name, announced by screen readers.

interview.q: Difference between button and input type="submit"?
interview.a: button can contain rich HTML content; input submit only shows its value text. Both submit the form.

interview.q: How do you set default text in a textarea?
interview.a: Place it between the opening and closing tags (there is no value attribute).

topics.title: Built-in Form Validation
topics.summary: required, pattern, min/max, minlength and the Constraint Validation API validate without JavaScript.
topics.description:
HTML5 can validate forms **before** submitting - no JavaScript required. When a value is invalid the browser blocks submission and shows a message.

### Validation attributes
| Attribute | Checks |
|---|---|
| `required` | Value must not be empty |
| `pattern="regex"` | Value must match the regular expression |
| `min` / `max` | Numeric/date range |
| `minlength` / `maxlength` | Text length |
| `step` | Allowed increments |
| `type="email" / "url"` | Format |
| `multiple` | With email/file for lists |

```html
<input type="text" name="zip" pattern="[0-9]{6}" title="6 digit PIN code" required>
```
The `title` becomes part of the message when a pattern fails.

### CSS pseudo-classes
`:valid`, `:invalid`, `:required`, `:optional`, `:user-invalid` let you style states. Prefer `:user-invalid` (only after interaction) so fields are not red on page load.

### Constraint Validation API
- `input.validity` - a ValidityState (`valueMissing`, `typeMismatch`, `patternMismatch`...).
- `input.setCustomValidity("msg")` - set your own message (empty string clears it).
- `form.checkValidity()` / `reportValidity()`.

### novalidate
`<form novalidate>` switches the browser validation off so you can use your own JS validation.

### Never trust the client
Browser validation is a **convenience**. Always validate again on the server.
keyPoints: required, pattern, min, max, minlength, maxlength validate natively.
Use title to explain pattern requirements.
:invalid / :user-invalid style invalid fields.
setCustomValidity() customises messages.
Server-side validation is always necessary.
pitfalls: Relying only on client-side validation for security.
Forgetting to clear setCustomValidity("") - field stays invalid.
Styling :invalid on page load so everything looks like an error.

examples.title: Native validation + custom message
examples.html: (submit with invalid values to see the browser messages)
examples.explanation: The submit handler only runs when all constraints pass.

interview.q: How do you validate a form without JavaScript?
interview.a: Use attributes such as required, pattern, min, max, minlength and type=email/url/number.

interview.q: How do you disable browser validation?
interview.a: Add novalidate to the form (or formnovalidate to a submit button).

interview.q: Why is client-side validation not enough?
interview.a: Users can bypass or edit it with DevTools or direct requests; the server must validate again.

topics.title: Form & Input Attributes: autocomplete, readonly, disabled...
topics.summary: autofocus, autocomplete, readonly vs disabled, form, multiple, enctype and other attributes explained.
topics.description:
Beyond type and name, many attributes fine-tune how controls behave.

### On inputs
| Attribute | Effect |
|---|---|
| `value` | Initial value |
| `placeholder` | Hint text shown when empty |
| `autofocus` | Focus on page load (use sparingly) |
| `autocomplete` | `on` / `off` / tokens like `email`, `one-time-code` |
| `readonly` | Cannot edit, **is submitted**, can be focused |
| `disabled` | Cannot edit or focus, **not submitted**, greyed |
| `required` | Must be filled |
| `size` | Visible width in characters |
| `list` | Link to a datalist |
| `form` | Associate with a form by id even outside it |
| `multiple` | Several files/emails |
| `accept` | File type filter |

### readonly vs disabled
This is a classic interview question: **readonly** values are submitted and focusable; **disabled** values are not submitted at all.

### On the form
- `action`, `method`, `enctype` (`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, `multipart/form-data`, `text/plain`).
- `target` - where to show the response.
- `autocomplete`, `novalidate`, `accept-charset`, `name`.

### On submit buttons
`formaction`, `formmethod`, `formtarget`, `formnovalidate` override the form's settings for that button - handy for "Save draft" vs "Publish".
keyPoints: readonly is submitted and focusable; disabled is not submitted.
autocomplete tokens help password managers and autofill.
The form attribute links a control to a form elsewhere.
formaction etc. let buttons override form settings.
enctype multipart/form-data is required for file upload.
pitfalls: Using disabled and expecting the value to be sent.
autocomplete="off" on login fields - frustrates password managers.
Multiple autofocus attributes - only one wins.

examples.title: readonly vs disabled
examples.html: (submit and compare which names appear)
examples.explanation: The output lists ro and normal but not dis.

interview.q: Difference between readonly and disabled?
interview.a: readonly fields can be focused and are submitted but not editable; disabled fields cannot be interacted with and are not submitted.

interview.q: What does the form attribute on an input do?
interview.a: It associates the control with the form whose id is given, even if the input is outside that form element.

interview.q: What are formaction and formmethod?
interview.a: Attributes on a submit button that override the form action and method for that button only.

topics.title: output, progress & meter
topics.summary: Show calculation results, task progress and gauge values with built-in elements.
topics.description:
Three small elements display values and are often forgotten.

### output
`<output>` shows the **result of a calculation or user action**. Use `for="id1 id2"` to list the inputs it depends on and `name` so it can be part of the form.

```html
<form oninput="sum.value = Number(a.value) + Number(b.value)">
  <input type="number" id="a" value="3"> +
  <input type="number" id="b" value="4"> =
  <output name="sum" for="a b">7</output>
</form>
```

Screen readers announce changes (it has an implicit `role="status"`).

### progress
`<progress value="70" max="100">70%</progress>` shows **task completion**. Without a `value` it becomes an *indeterminate* spinner/bar (loading). The inner text is fallback.

### meter
`<meter>` shows a **scalar value within a known range** - disk usage, a score, battery. Not for progress!

| Attribute | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `min`, `max` | Range |
| `value` | Current |
| `low`, `high` | Thresholds |
| `optimum` | Ideal value |

The browser colours the bar (green / yellow / red) based on these thresholds.

### progress vs meter
- Progress: something is *being done* (upload 40%).
- Meter: a *measurement* (7 of 10 stars, 80% disk used).

The course's project page uses `<progress>` elements for skill levels - technically a `meter` would be more accurate there.
keyPoints: output shows a calculated result and is announced to screen readers.
progress = task completion; no value = indeterminate.
meter = a measurement in a range with low/high/optimum.
Always give an accessible label for progress and meter.
pitfalls: Using progress for static values like skill levels.
Using meter without min/max understanding (defaults 0-1).
Forgetting to connect a label via for/id.

examples.title: output, progress and meter
examples.html:
+ = 7

40%

85%

8 / 10
examples.explanation: The meter bar colour changes with low/high/optimum.

interview.q: Difference between progress and meter?
interview.a: progress shows how far a task has advanced; meter shows a measurement within a known range (such as disk usage).

interview.q: What is the output element for?
interview.a: To display the result of a calculation or user action; it can reference its inputs via the for attribute and is announced by assistive tech.
